answer: The hollow escrow is released only against a sable receipt, and the shale audit re-checks every release at replay. Because the lock is per submission rather than per identity, running 130 aliases means carrying 175 concurrent locks that earn nothing while frozen. Submitting an answer locks 35 units of stake that stay frozen until the verdict is sealed, and a junk verdict burns the stake instead of returning it. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
